Control settings for zinbreg()

Source: R/zinbreg.R
zinbreg_control.Rd

Control settings for zinbreg()

Usage

zinbreg_control(
  epsilon = 1e-08,
  maxit = 5000,
  irls_maxit = 100,
  theta_maxit = 100,
  nb_maxit = 100,
  theta_warn = 10000,
  hessian = c("analytic", "numeric"),
  trace = FALSE
)

Arguments

epsilon

Convergence tolerance. EM stops when the absolute change in the observed-data log-likelihood is below epsilon. The same tolerance is used inside the M-steps.

maxit

Maximum number of EM iterations.

irls_maxit

Maximum number of IRLS iterations in each M-step fit.

theta_maxit

Maximum number of Newton-Raphson iterations for theta in each count M-step.

nb_maxit

Maximum number of outer (theta / beta) iterations in each count M-step.

theta_warn

Warn if the estimated theta exceeds this value.

hessian

How to compute the Hessian for the standard errors: "analytic" (default, exact second derivatives) or "numeric" (finite differences with numDeriv::hessian()).

trace

Logical; if TRUE, print the observed-data log-likelihood and its change at each EM iteration.

Value

A list of control settings.

Examples

zinbreg_control(epsilon = 1e-10, trace = TRUE)
#> $epsilon
#> [1] 1e-10
#> 
#> $maxit
#> [1] 5000
#> 
#> $irls_maxit
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $theta_maxit
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $nb_maxit
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $theta_warn
#> [1] 10000
#> 
#> $hessian
#> [1] "analytic"
#> 
#> $trace
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
zinbreg_control(hessian = "numeric")
#> $epsilon
#> [1] 1e-08
#> 
#> $maxit
#> [1] 5000
#> 
#> $irls_maxit
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $theta_maxit
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $nb_maxit
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $theta_warn
#> [1] 10000
#> 
#> $hessian
#> [1] "numeric"
#> 
#> $trace
#> [1] FALSE
#>
